feature: MQTT inbound QoS 2 publisher persistence cache

baseline.head: d1c15a7412abd9edcb4e03222205c7631075e199
baseline.equivalence: src/mqtt is byte-identical between mqtt_source_commit and head

reference.observation: Mosquitto keeps connection Session state local to its single event-loop owner; netz instead permits concurrent connection tasks and protects the Session Store globally

objective: Avoid resolving stable route id to Session and reading expiry on each inbound QoS 2 PUBLISH and PUBREL when the generation-checked live ClientSlot already caches session_persistent.

publish_and_pubrel.design: A shared helper validates connection slot generation, returns ClientSlot.state.session_persistent, and retains the original Store lookup for stale or non-connection identities. Both inbound QoS 2 stages use it.
publish_and_pubrel.focused_tests: Debug and ReleaseFast durability, Session, and live QoS 2 filters passed 125/125
publish_and_pubrel.rejection_reason: The small instruction reduction did not translate to cycles: median cycles regressed 0.72% and the candidate won only 2/8 pairs. Timing improvements cannot override the fixed PMU guard.

publish_only.design: PUBLISH reuses the ClientSlot already required immediately afterward and checks Store equivalence only in debug assertions. PUBREL retains the original Store lookup; there is no new helper or fallback branch.
publish_only.focused_tests: Debug and ReleaseFast durability, Session, and live QoS 2 filters passed 125/125
publish_only.rejection_reason: The narrower path regressed instructions 0.32%, cycles 0.29%, p50 2.89%, and p99 1.45% by paired medians. It failed both PMU guards despite noisy throughput improvement.

benchmark_method.excluded_probe: An earlier set without an explicit post-attach wait undercounted the first baseline instruction arm by about 6% and was excluded before making a decision.

preserved_invariants: durable incoming QoS 2 state commits before PUBREC
PUBREL removal and routing commit before PUBCOMP
exactly-once release and Message Expiry use one atomic persistence transaction
Client ID takeover and stale generations retain the original Store lookup semantics
ClientSlot, Pending, and transmission layouts are unchanged

final_state.follow_up: Do not add slot-generation or fallback selection merely to replace these Store lookups. Target a larger scheduling, locking, or ownership boundary and keep instructions plus cycles as mandatory guards.
